description: Mother Ash meets you at the bottom of the Lowvents stair with a shovel, which she hands you, and a slate, which she does not. On the slate are the Stokers' shifts for the Foundry fires: names, hours, and a column of Crowns paid against each. The names run down the slate. The Crowns do not run very far at all. "You asked who it belongs to," she says. "Start by finding out who does it."

options.label: Take a shift on the Lowvents' own furnace, and feed it till the shift bell.

success.text: Eight hours. By the third your arms belong to somebody else; by the sixth the furnace has a temper you can read. At the bell, Mother Ash chalks your name on the slate below the others and writes nothing against it in the Crowns column. "Fellowship doesn't pay," she says. "It counts." Walking home, you smell of coal and do not mind, which is new.

failure.text: By the fourth hour the furnace door has had more of your forearm than you would like. Mother Ash takes the shovel back without comment, and somebody else finishes your shift. Your name does not go on the slate today.

options.label: Take the slate to Silas Tallow and ask what the House pays a Stoker.

success.text: "Two Crowns a shift, less the House's commission," says Silas Tallow, "which is a very fair rate for work nobody else will do." He tells you the price of coal, of bread and of a Lowvents lease, all without being asked. By the time he finishes, you have worked out that a Stoker's week buys a Stoker's week, and not an hour more. He sees you do the sum, and smiles.

options.label: Tell Mother Ash the Gazette had the columns first, and ask whether the Lowvents believed them.

success.text: "Believed them?" Mother Ash takes the slate back. "We read the Gazette to see what the Board wants us to think. Then we look out of the window." She shows you the bottom rim, where every family has a mark scratched in the brick, a hand's width apart, each a year newer than the last. Nobody in the Lowvents needed Hester to tell them. They needed someone to write it down where Gaugehill would see.
